w: Sousse's walled old town encloses a kasbah, fortifications and the Great Mosque, a textbook example of early Islamic urban architecture in the Maghreb. Punic funerary steles turned up between the Ribat and the Great Mosque during 19th- and 20th-century digs. It also houses the Archaeological Museum.
s: A walled old town built around a kasbah and ribat
_facts: encompasses a kasbah, fortifications and the Great Mosque

w: Commissioned in 851 by the Aghlabid ruler Abu al-Abbas Muhammad al-Aghlabi, vassal of the Abbasid Caliphate, this is a major monument of early Aghlabid religious architecture on the Tunisian coast. Its prayer hall was expanded more than once in later centuries, without erasing its 9th-century core.
s: A 9th-century Aghlabid mosque on the Tunisian coast
_facts: commissioned by Aghlabid ruler Abu al-Abbas Muhammad al-Aghlabi
prayer hall expanded multiple times over the centuries

w: Housed in a palace that once belonged to a family of aristocrats in the medina of Sousse, this small museum recreates daily domestic life in the city during the 18th and 19th centuries, its rooms furnished as they might have looked under Ottoman-era Tunisian rule rather than laid out as display cases.
s: A private palace turned into a house of daily life
_facts: housed in a palace belonging to an aristocratic family
